Question Choices: A triangle has angles 90 degrees and 33 degrees. Find the third angle. Enter only the angle measure in degrees.
Solution: Triangle interior angles sum to 180 degrees. The known angles total 90 + 33 = 123, leaving 180 - 123 = 57 degrees.

Question Choices: An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of 100 degrees. Find each base angle. Enter only the angle measure in degrees.
Hints: The base angles are congruent.|They share 180 - 100 equally.
Solution: The base angles opposite the equal sides are equal. Together they measure 180 - 100 = 80 degrees, so each is 80/2 = 40 degrees.

Question Choices: An isosceles triangle has a base angle of 45 degrees. Find the vertex angle. Enter only the angle measure in degrees.
Solution: Both base angles measure 45 degrees. Their total is 90, leaving vertex angle 180 - 90 = 90 degrees.

Question Choices: Select. Can a triangle have two 95-degree angles? ~~Yes | No~~
Solution: No. Two 95-degree angles alone total 190 degrees, already greater than the 180-degree triangle total. A third positive angle cannot make a triangle.

Question Choices: Select. An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of which angles? ~~One adjacent and one remote interior angle | The two remote interior angles | All three interior angles~~
Hints: Use the exterior angle theorem.|The angles not adjacent to the exterior angle.
Solution: The exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle sum to 180 degrees. All three interior angles also sum to 180. Subtracting the adjacent interior angle shows that the exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote (nonadjacent) interior angles.
